issues.title: feat(staff): compute engineers are people, not an integer (#1247)
issues.body:
Closes #1247. **Ladder-Impact: bump — this wants an epoch boundary, not a mid-week merge.** See the last section.

Found by Pip playing the v0.14.2 release build: *"When I acquire a startup, my employee screen tells me I have 2 engineers but they don't load into the sim."* His screen, in **one frame**:

```
Team Size: 1 employees
* Safety Researchers: 1
* Compute Engineers: 2
```

Ruled 2026-08-22: *"real STAFF, but they might not eg produce as much research?"*

## The root cause

`get_total_staff()` **switched models** — objects when any `Researcher` existed, legacy integers otherwise. So the instant a player hired one real person, everyone who was only ever an integer **stopped counting**, while the screens went on printing those integers beside the total.

Worse than a display bug: `desks_free` derives from it, so staff that didn't count **occupied no desks**. Acquisition was a route around the office cap that #791's early economy treats as a real constraint, and the 8/9/10-employee warnings never fired for them.

## What changed

`Researcher.SPECIALIZATIONS` gains `compute_engineer` — that table already carried per-role output profiles, so this extends an existing shape. `research_speed_modifier: 0.35`.

**That 0.35 is not a balance proposal.** It's the first nonzero contribution they've ever had. Before this they produced **nothing** — no research, no compute, no doom effect — while still drawing a stationery bill and counting toward doom totals. `hire_compute_engineer` was an action that cost money and delivered a stationery bill, which is the shape **#595** is about.

`acquire_startup` and `hire_compute_engineer` create people via `add_researcher()`, the same seam the hiring pipeline uses, so acquired staff are indistinguishable downstream: desks, roster, burnout, firing, warnings. Seeded RNG only — replays stay deterministic.

## Two more instances found *by* the failing tests

Three existing tests went red on my first attempt. **Reading them rather than fixing them** turned up two real defects:

- **`emergency_pivot` converted counters, not people.** It moved `capability_researchers → safety_researchers` while the actual objects stayed on their old lane — so a "converted" researcher kept producing capabilities research *and* capabilities doom while the counters said otherwise.
- **`resource_accessor.gd`** carried *"Compute engineers use legacy count only (no Researcher object)"* — true when written, and it's the channel **event content** uses. So `+2 compute_engineers` from an event minted staff the sim couldn't see.

## Why `max()` and not either model alone

My first attempt returned `researchers.size() + managers` absolutely. That broke three tests **correctly** — a legacy salary-billing fallback that `test_turn_manager.gd` explicitly documents sets counters with no objects.

The counters and objects are two **views of the same people**. `add_researcher`/`remove_researcher` keep them in lockstep, so in any state the game can now produce they're **equal** and `max()` is a no-op. They diverge in exactly one direction — a legacy path that set a counter without a person. A plain **sum** would double-count the synced case; **either model alone** is how this bug happened.

## Tests

```
before: 1396 tests, 0 failures
after:  1403 tests, 0 failures, 137/137 files, 91s
```

Seven new, verified **by name** in the JUnit XML. Two encode the screenshot directly: role counters must **sum** to headcount, and acquired staff must **occupy desks**.

## Still open, deliberately

What a compute engineer **positively does** — cut compute upkeep, raise capacity, gate an infrastructure action — is the design question this ruling opens and is **not answered here**. It's recorded as an open question in the code rather than guessed at. The hiring pipeline (#1225) still can't offer one. **Managers are still a bare integer — the next instance of this same seam.**

## Merge timing

Ladder-Impact: **bump**. Desk pressure, headcount warnings and research throughput all move, so an L5 score and a post-change score are not comparable. This should land at an epoch cut, **not** mid-week onto the board blessed 2026-08-21. `check_ladder_bump.py --owed` will show the debt until an epoch pays it.

issues.title: tools: scan closed issues whose own acceptance criteria nobody recorded checking
issues.body:
Pip, 2026-08-22, on finding #775 closed `COMPLETED` with one of its three acceptance criteria unmet and no comment recording it: *"How do we scan for anything else closed with zero comments that might have partially completed work? ew. shadow tech debt is gross."*

## Measured, over 426 closed issues

```
closed with zero comments      159   (37% -- far too coarse to act on)
  carrying unticked checkboxes  18
  carrying prose criteria       28
```

Scoped to the Godot era (`--since 700`):

```
closed with zero comments       31
  carrying checkboxes            0
  carrying prose criteria        2   <- #775 and #720
```

## Five checked by hand. Four were satisfied.

| Issue | Criterion | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| #488 | "at least 5 test cases covering core doom" | 27 + 18 exist |
| #481 | "in-game What's New modal" | `whats_new_modal.gd`, wired |
| #531 | "no Node-20 deprecation annotations" | 54 actions on `@v7` |
| #720 | "first-launch help layer" | `welcome_overlay.gd` exists |
| **#775** | **CI understands `release/*`** | **genuinely unmet -> #1269** |

**#720 is the interesting one.** Its criterion said gate on `games_played == 0`; the implementation deliberately did *not*, with the reason written at `game_config.gd:702` — `increment_games_played()` runs *before* the intro routes, which would break that test. The criterion was improved on, and the improvement was recorded. **That is what a healthy miss looks like.**

## The negative result is the useful part

Across all 18 issues carrying unticked checkboxes, the number of **ticked** boxes is **zero**. Not low — zero. Checkboxes have never been live state in this repo; they're spec text. So *"unticked box in a closed issue"* carries **no information** here.

The tool reports that population separately, prints the zero, and says to **re-measure rather than trust the conclusion forever** — if someone starts ticking boxes, the signal becomes real.

## What it will not do

It does not say whether work was done — it *cannot*, the criteria are prose. It produces a shortlist for a human, and the shortlist is only useful **because it is short**. The header prints the measured hit rate so the next reader expects mostly-satisfied rather than mostly-debt.

Exit **2** on a failed fetch, distinct from exit 0 with an empty shortlist: *"the scan could not run"* and *"the scan found nothing"* must not look alike (#640).

## Encoding, measured

`subprocess` with `text=True` decodes using the ANSI codepage on Windows. Issue bodies aren't cp1252 and the first run died on byte `0x8f` — the **good** failure. Now explicit utf-8 with `errors="replace"`, so one stray byte costs one grep match rather than the whole scan.

Ladder-Impact: none — read-only reporting tool; nothing under `godot/`.

issues.title: RELEASING.md says ship from a release branch; four releases shipped from main and CI has no release/* handling
issues.body:
`RELEASING.md` says "ship from the release branch, never from churny `main`". Four releases have shipped from `main`, and the CI workflow has no `release/*` handling at all.

## The protocol

`RELEASING.md` -- **ACTIVE PROTOCOL, ratified 2026-07-25 (#775)**:

> **Each monthly epoch, cut a release branch.** At the epoch (1st Friday), cut `release/v0.X` from the epoch commit and tag `v0.X.0`. That branch is the stable line for the whole month.
>
> **Ship from the release branch, never from churny `main`.** Builds and tags come off `release/v0.X`; `main` keeps absorbing the next epoch's work.

## What is actually true

    git ls-remote --heads origin 'release/*'   -> (nothing)

v0.13.0, v0.13.1, v0.13.2, v0.14.0, v0.14.1 and v0.14.2 were all tagged off `main`. **The release-branch half of this protocol has never been exercised.**

`#775`'s own acceptance list had three items:

| Criterion | State |
|---|---|
| hotpatch criteria list written | DONE -- `RELEASING.md`, four numbered criteria |
| RELEASING.md documents the flow | DONE -- 64 lines, clear |
| **CI release workflow understands `release/*` branches** | **NOT DONE** |

`.github/workflows/enhanced-release.yml` triggers on `push: tags: 'v*.*.*'` plus `workflow_dispatch`. There is no `release/*` branch trigger, no branch-aware build path, and nothing that distinguishes a tag cut from a release branch from a tag cut from `main`.

#775 was closed COMPLETED on 2026-07-25 with **no comments**, so nothing recorded that the third criterion was outstanding.

## Why this is worth doing before September

`docs/ROADMAP.md` puts **v0.15 on Sep 4** -- the next monthly epoch, and the first cut where the protocol says a `release/v0.15` branch must exist. Discovering on epoch night that the release workflow does not recognise the branch is a bad evening, and epoch nights already carry the [Gate 4]/[Gate 5]/[Gate 6] ceremony and a hard 17:30 stop.

The failure mode is not subtle but it IS late-breaking: the tag fires the workflow, the workflow builds whatever it is pointed at, and nobody finds out the branch was irrelevant until someone asks which commit shipped.

## Suggested scope

1. Teach `enhanced-release.yml` about `release/*` -- at minimum, verify that a tag being built is reachable from the expected release branch, and say so in the build summary.
2. **Rehearse it once before Sep 4.** Cut a throwaway `release/v0.14-rehearsal` from the v0.14.2 tag, push a `v0.14.2-rc` style tag, watch the workflow, delete both. A protocol that has never been run is a hypothesis.
3. Record the outcome in `RELEASING.md`'s worked-example section, which currently documents v0.13 -- a release that predates the protocol.

## Not in scope

The trunk model itself is settled and correct: `main` is trunk, `main` IS the stash, no `develop` (ADR-0001). Nothing here reopens that. This is only about the release-branch half never having been wired up or run.

Found while checking whether a long-lived feature branch was permitted for #1247. It is not -- the protocol is explicit -- and reading it surfaced this.

issues.title: AK1004: fix the four organisation-line hits, exempt the rule-stating file, teach the guard proper nouns
issues.body:
**Routed from the 2026-08-22 memo pass.** Ruled by Pip this morning, `capture:e39dae1e` (06:36), reading review sheet `certes/2026-08-21/073141`.

## The ruling, verbatim

> *"AK1004 — I would like to, one, fix the four genuine ones in the organisation line, and then two, exempt the file that states the rule and teach the guard very carefully about capitalised proper nouns."*

## Three acts

1. **Fix the four genuine hits** in the organisation-line guard's output.
2. **Exempt the file that states the rule.** A guard that flags the document defining its own rule is generating a permanent false positive — the same pattern `certes/CLAUDE.md` handles with an explicit exemption for rule-stating files.
3. **Teach the guard about capitalised proper nouns**, and Pip's emphasis was on *"very carefully"*. The underlying rule is Australian/UK spelling estate-wide (*"organisation with an S"*, ruled 2026-08-12) — but a proper noun that happens to contain the American spelling is not a violation. Getting this wrong in the tightening direction makes the guard noisy; getting it wrong in the loosening direction makes it useless.

The rest of that sheet's rulings are in `coordination/TRIAGE_2026-08-22_memo-pass.md` §1 and were answered on `coordination#85`.

issues.title: The league cycle handbook Pip asked to update does not appear to exist -- name it or rule create-vs-update
issues.body:
**Routed from the 2026-08-22 memo pass**, `capture:adf65cc3`, with a correction the seat could not resolve.

## What Pip said

> *"The one thing that has gone stale and is worth 10 minutes later — the league cycle handbook. Oh, great, there is a handbook. Let's update the league cycle handbook, because I bet that that is very prosy and has very few things decided and mechanically determined. And I reckon that is going to be a big source of drift if we don't deal with it."*

## The problem: it does not exist

Searched `coordination`, `pdoom1`, `pdoom-data`, `pdoom1-website` for any file matching *league cycle handbook*. **The only hits are the two documents written this morning that quote the instruction itself.** No handbook file was found.

So one of three things is true, and this repo is better placed than coordination to say which:

1. It exists under a different name — if so, **name it and this becomes the 10-minute update Pip expected**.
2. It never existed, and he is remembering a plan to write one — in which case this is a create, not an update, and it should inherit the mechanical-derivation requirement from the playbook issue.
3. It exists outside git.

**Do not create a new prose handbook without resolving this first.** His stated concern is precisely that a prosy handbook with few things mechanically determined becomes a source of drift — writing a fresh one by hand would deliver the defect he is trying to avoid.

issues.title: Create the PDoom release-cycle playbook + check sheet, derived mechanically, used weekly
issues.body:
**Routed from the 2026-08-22 memo pass.** Ruled by Pip this morning, `capture:adf65cc3` (walking memo, 06:42), reading the ledger-row protocol.

## What he asked for

> *"I want those recorded in, like, I suppose, the playbook or the play-sheet for PDoom release cycles, which, if it doesn't exist, I would like to have it created as something that is derived mostly mechanically through mechanisms so that we know it can be updated. And then this can be a combination of a playbook and check sheet that I can start using every week."*

Three properties, all load-bearing:
- **A combined playbook + check sheet**, used weekly by Pip himself
- **Derived mostly mechanically** — not hand-maintained prose. This is §5i (*derive indexes, never hand-maintain them*) applied to a procedure.
- It absorbs the **ledger-row protocol etiquette** he had just read and approved: *"I'm glad to read the etiquette things."*

## The cadence to encode

His words, and the ordering is the point:

> *"figure out the order of the cadence between, like, decide what I'm going to do on PDoom data, push that, decide what I'm going to do on PDoom itself, and then decide what I'm going to do on PDoom website and push that. So it's probably something like **data feeds into game, game feeds into website, website feeds into the universe**."*

## Related, filed separately

The league cycle handbook he asked to update in the same memo **does not appear to exist** — see the sibling issue. Do not silently create it under this one.

issues.title: guards: 15 running in pre-commit and nowhere else, and wired gates with no self-test
issues.body:
**Routed from the 2026-08-22 memo pass** (`coordination/TRIAGE_2026-08-22_memo-pass.md` §1). Pip ruled this by voice on 2026-08-20 20:11, `capture:c5381714`, and it has not reached this repo until now.

## The ruling, verbatim

> *"I'm reading the guard order and I would like there to be a work — so 15 guards running in pre-commit and nowhere else is clearly wrong, and then they have a bunch of wired gates have no self-test which is against our own doctrine. So I would like to see... for those guards and those wired gates, I think we can just do those as two light bursts of work. I don't actually really want to see a plan or any triaging. I just think they can all be solved, but I'm going to leave the mechanism by which that happens open to self-direction."*

## Two acts

1. **Guards that run in pre-commit and nowhere else.** Pip's words: *"clearly wrong."* A pre-commit hook is per-clone and bypassable with `--no-verify`; a guard that exists only there is not installed on any machine that has not run the install step.
2. **Wired gates with no self-test.** Against this estate's own doctrine — §5g requires a guard to have been observed RED, with the run id recorded, before it counts as installed. A gate that has only ever passed is indistinguishable from one that cannot fail.

## How Pip wants this done — read this before replying

**He explicitly does not want a plan and does not want triage.** *"I don't actually really want to see a plan or any triaging... two light bursts of work... mechanism open to self-direction."*

A reply that opens with a proposed sequencing document has misread the ruling. Do the work, then say what changed.

Source: `capture:c5381514` → corrected: `capture:c5381714`. Context in `coordination/GUARD_AUDIT_2026-08-19.md` if it helps scope the 15.

issues.title: feat(music): nudging the conductor, and stop dropping picks made mid-crossfade (#1249)
issues.body:
Closes #1249.

Pip, 2026-08-21: *"I would probably like the game to tell me it's switching tracks if I select another one and it doesn't start within, like, half a second. Make it diegetic -- 'nudging the conductor....'"*

## Two causes, one symptom, and only one was cosmetic

**1. The crossfade is 2s and starts silent.** `CROSSFADE_DURATION = 2.0`, incoming player at `-80 dB`. A pick is inaudible for roughly the first half-second **by design**. Nothing broken — the player just can't tell "working on it" from "my click did nothing".

**2. A pick made *during* a crossfade was discarded:**

```gdscript
if is_crossfading:
    print("[MusicManager] Already crossfading, ignoring request")
    return
```

Crossfades last 2s, so **any second pick inside that window was silently lost**, with a `print()` as its only trace. That's the silent-wrongness failure this codebase hunts everywhere else — `player_status_line()` carries a comment about not blaming the player for a state they didn't cause, a few lines from where this was happening to them.

**Fixing only (1) would have been worse than nothing:** the nudge would appear and then resolve to the *wrong track*.

## What changed

The line is Pip's, verbatim, and **takes precedence over everything else** in `player_status_line()`. During a switch, reporting the old track as "now playing" is exactly how a player concludes their click did nothing.

Mid-crossfade picks are **queued**, newest only — four clicks in two seconds means "play the fourth", not "play all four in order". Applied when the running crossfade completes; the pending/nudge flags survive that hop, because from the player's side the pick still hasn't landed.

## A flag, not a clock

A one-shot timer sets `_conductor_nudging`; `player_status_line()` reads the flag and stays the documented *"pure string build, unit-tested"*. Tests set it directly rather than sleeping half a second — **and one test asserts that property**, so if this ever needs a real timer to pass, someone finds out the function stopped being unit-testable.

`_switch_pending` and `_conductor_nudging` are separate on purpose: a switch landing in 300ms **never flickers a message**. Only one still waiting speaks up.

## Tests

Five, verified **by name in the JUnit XML** rather than inferred from a total:

```
pass  test_nudge_line_takes_precedence_over_now_playing
pass  test_no_nudge_when_nothing_is_pending
pass  test_status_line_stays_a_pure_state_to_string_map
pass  test_a_pick_during_a_crossfade_is_queued_not_dropped
pass  test_only_the_newest_queued_pick_survives

before: 1396 tests, 0 failures
after:  1401 tests, 0 failures, 136/136 files, 92s
```

Ladder-Impact: none — music is a pure view-layer side-effect (ADR-0006) and track selection is explicitly not a state mutation (`test_adaptive_music.gd`: *"playing a different track is not a state mutation and must not unrank the run"*).

issues.title: Acquired startup staff half-exist: they consume stationery and move doom, but occupy no desks and cannot be managed
issues.body:
Acquiring a startup grants staff that half-exist: they consume stationery and move doom, but occupy no desks, have no productivity, and cannot be managed.

Found by Pip in a live v0.14.2-rc run (`01d40168`), 2026-08-21: *"When I acquire a startup, my employee screen tells me I have 2 engineers but they don't load into the sim."* The Employee Management screen showed **Team Size: 1** and **Compute Engineers: 2** in the same frame, with rows `#2` and `#3` rendering a description but no Skill Level or Productivity, while `#1 Iris Wilson` had both.

## Root cause

`godot/scripts/core/actions.gd:712-731` -- `acquire_startup` bumps LEGACY INTEGER COUNTERS and never creates a `Researcher` object:

```gdscript
match staff_type:
    0: state.safety_researchers += 2
    1: state.capability_researchers += 2
    2: state.compute_engineers += 2
```

Nothing is appended to `state.researchers`.

The two numbers on screen come from two different models:

- `godot/scripts/ui/employee_screen.gd:105` -- `Team Size` reads `state.total_staff`
- `godot/scripts/ui/employee_screen.gd:107-113` -- the role rows read `state.compute_engineers` etc. directly

and `godot/scripts/core/game_state.gd:795` switches models the instant one real researcher exists:

```gdscript
func get_total_staff() -> int:
    if researchers.size() > 0:
        return researchers.size() + managers      # 1
    return safety_researchers + capability_researchers + compute_engineers + managers  # 3
```

So with 1 hired researcher and 2 acquired engineers: object model says 1, counter model says 3, and both are printed side by side.

## Why this is not only a display defect

The phantom staff are read by some systems and not others, so they are half-real:

| System | Reads | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| `turn_manager.gd:374` | `compute_engineers` | They DO consume stationery |
| `doom_system.gd:196` | `safety + capability + compute_engineers` | They DO move doom |
| `game_state.gd:1455` | `office_hire_cap - get_total_staff()` | They occupy NO desks -- acquisition can exceed the office cap |
| `employee_screen.gd:_update_stats` | `researchers[]` | No productivity; never counted productive or unproductive |
| `employee_screen.gd:_update_warnings` | `total_staff` | The 8/9/10-employee management warnings never fire for them |
| `resource_accessor.gd:81` | -- | Comment states it outright: `# Compute engineers use legacy count only (no Researcher object)` |

The desk one is the sharpest: **acquisition is a route around the office hire cap**, which the early-economy design (#791) treats as a real constraint.

## Age and blast radius

Present since `2f803e46` (2025-10-31, "Doom momentum system + researcher specializations") -- the commit that introduced the `Researcher` object alongside the counters and never migrated `acquire_startup`. NOT a v0.14.2 regression; `actions.gd` and `employee_screen.gd` are untouched between `v0.14.1` and `01d40168`. It ships in every public build to date.

## Options, not a decision

1. **Make acquisition create Researcher objects.** The honest fix. Needs a spec answer for compute engineers, which have never had objects (`resource_accessor.gd:81`) -- so either they get objects too, or acquisition of a compute startup grants something else.
2. **Make `get_total_staff()` stop switching models** -- always `researchers.size() + legacy_counts + managers`. Cheap, makes the screen self-consistent, but leaves staff who cannot be assigned or burned out.
3. **Display-only:** label legacy counts as something other than employees. Cheapest, and it makes the game honest without pretending the sim changed.

Related seam: #1227 (the ledger and research progress stop at the edge of the roster) and #1226 (firing exists on a screen the player never reaches) are the same hybrid-model boundary showing up in different surfaces. Worth deciding the model once rather than three times.

## Ladder note

A fix to option 1 or 2 changes run outcomes (desk pressure, doom totals) and would be `Ladder-Impact: bump`. Option 3 would not.

issues.title: fix(game-over): stop blaming crises the player survived (#1248)
issues.body:
Closes #1248. Found by Pip playing the v0.14.2 release build.

His defeat screen read:

```
CAUSE OF DEATH
  t80 funding_starvation payroll (cash@ 248.0, bills 670.3)
  t87 rep_collapse reputation (rep@ 5.0)
```

The run ended on **turn 130 with $1,189,765 in the bank.** He didn't die of the turn-80 cash crisis — he **survived** it and recovered by three orders of magnitude. The screen told him otherwise at the exact moment he was looking for an explanation.

## Both guards already existed in that file

`death_attribution.gd` states the rule in its own header — *"a default RECENT_WINDOW+ turns before death is history, not cause"* — and classifies `funding_starvation`/`rep_collapse` as cascade **watermarks**, *"which mark the chain but aren't damage"*.

`classify()` used `RECENT_WINDOW` for its own ledger verdict. **`chain_summary()` never did — and that's what the panel prints.**

t80 and t87 are **50 and 43 turns** before death. Outside the window by a factor of three, and both watermark kinds.

`funding_starvation` compounds it: one-shot-per-episode, **resets on recovery**, but the `cause_log` entry is permanent. Recovering from a cash crisis clears the flag and leaves the tombstone.

## The fix

`chain_split()` uses the `RECENT_WINDOW` that was already there. The panel shows proximate causes under **CAUSE OF DEATH** and the rest under **EARLIER IN THE RUN — *survived, not fatal***.

**Nothing is dropped.** The t80/t87 trail is genuinely interesting; it just isn't the cause.

`classify()` returns `chain_proximate`/`chain_earlier` **alongside** `chain`, which is deliberately unchanged — `tests/manual/l1_month_driver.gd`, `test_exploit_sweep.gd` and `test_l1_month_sweep.gd` analyse whole runs and want every cause.

## Two edge cases, decided rather than left to fall out

- **Everything too old to blame** → the panel says *"nothing recent enough to blame"*, not a bare heading or history promoted to fill space.
- **A cause with no turn stamp** → treated as **proximate**. It can't be *shown* to be old, and demoting it would hide a real one. The filter fails toward blaming, not toward silence.

## Tests

Five, built from the actual run — including a **control**: the same shapes logged at t128 **must still be blamed**. A filter that hid everything would pass a test that only checks the bug is gone.

```
before: 1396 tests, 0 failures
after:  1401 tests, 0 failures, 136/136 files, 95s
```

Ladder-Impact: none — `classify()`'s `surface`, `root_cause` and `chain` are unchanged (`chain_summary` was refactored to share a line-builder, same output); the new keys are read only by the game-over panel; the module is read-only over a finished state and touches no scoring, run-outcome or replay path.

issues.title: P6 needs a mechanism or deletion: the worktree rule was broken by an agent on 2026-08-21
issues.body:
**Drafted 2026-08-21 by the pdoom1-website seat. Mechanism designed and MEASURED in a throwaway repo, not built here. This is a ruling request, and it carries its own deletion trigger.**

Raised because P6's falsifier fired on 2026-08-21: an agent performed six checkouts and a `git reset --hard` in the shared main checkout while another seat was working there. See `docs/POSTMORTEM_2026-08-07_CAPTURE.md` section 6a.

# P6: give the rule a mechanism, or delete it

For Pip. Measured today on git 2.52.0.windows.1 / Git Bash, not recalled; no
repo file modified.

## 1. The decision

P6 reads "No agent operates in the main checkout; lanes get worktrees." Its
falsifier fired: `git reflog` in `D:/Local_Code/pdoom1` shows six
`checkout: moving from X to Y` plus one `reset: moving to origin/main` between
05:20 and 05:59 UTC today, while another seat held work in that tree. Nothing
was lost only because that work sat on a branch. It built an isolated worktree four hours
later once it noticed staged work, so the rule is operable, just not operated. A rule broken and kept reads as a control
in every future audit. Choose: **(a)** wire the mechanism below, or **(b)**
delete P6.

## 2. Detection — read this before the candidates

**Retrospective attribution is impossible here, which kills any audit-shaped
mechanism outright.** Measured:

| Source | Agent vs Pip | Discriminates? |
|---|---|---|
| reflog ident `%gn/%ge`, author `%an/%ae`, message `%gs` | byte-identical | **No** |
| `$CLAUDECODE`, `$AI_AGENT` | `1` / `claude-code_2-1-233_agent` vs unset | **Yes, live only** |

The reflog stores no environment. So P6's own falsifier — "read `git reflog`...
any agent-attributable reset" — **is not machine-checkable as written**; today's attribution came
from session context, not git. A mechanism must therefore fire *at
the moment of the operation*, inside the process running git. Both vars reach
hook processes (verified); neither survives into history.

## 3. Candidates

**M1 — `reference-transaction` hook, blocking.** *Detects:* any ref write by a process
carrying `$CLAUDECODE`/`$AI_AGENT`, main checkout only (`git rev-parse
--git-dir` equals `--git-common-dir` only there). *Lives:* `.git/hooks/reference-transaction`,
hand-installed — the pre-commit framework does **not** support this hook type,
the one place "extend what exists" fails. *Measured:* agent
`checkout` and agent `reset --hard` both exit 128 with HEAD unmoved; agent
commit inside a linked worktree exits 0; **human** checkout exits 0.
*Cost:* the naive form also blocks `git worktree add` — the remedy it demands —
and `fetch`; the tuned form allows `refs/remotes/*`, `ORIG_HEAD`, `AUTO_MERGE`,
`refs/stash` and a `PDOOM1_MAIN_CHECKOUT_OK=1` hatch (retested, all four cases
correct). Per-checkout, inert until installed. *Forced failure:* feed it a `HEAD` line on stdin with `CLAUDECODE=1`, assert
exit 1; repeat under `env -u CLAUDECODE -u AI_AGENT`, assert exit 0.

**M2 — `post-checkout` tripwire, detection only.** *Detects:* an agent-attributed branch
switch, logged to a ledger `quality-checks.yml` asserts is empty. *Lives:* a
`stages: [post-checkout]` entry beside `class-cache-check`, which already
installs that stage — genuinely extends what exists. *Cost:* **measured — `post-checkout` never fires on `git reset --hard`.**
Today's incident contained one hard reset, so M2 is blind to the most dangerous
of the seven operations, and fires after the damage. *Forced failure:*
invoke with synthetic SHAs and `CLAUDECODE=1`, assert non-zero.

**M3 — delete P6**, replaced by: "agents must not `reset` a tree they did not
create."

## 4. Weakest, and whether deletion wins

**M2 is weakest; do not build it** — it cannot see resets, the whole of today's
risk. **Deletion is not right:** the rule is not aspirational, and M1 was built
and made to both block and permit in about ten minutes. But delete P6 if M1 is
not installed this week — an uninstalled hook plus a written rule is worse than
no rule, because it adds the appearance of enforcement.

**Honest limit: M1 is a tripwire, not a cage.** An agent that hits the refusal
can export `PDOOM1_MAIN_CHECKOUT_OK=1`; one that edits files can delete the
hook. It turns a silent slip into a loud deliberate act — and today's incident *was*
an unnoticed slip, so it is aimed at the observed failure mode, not an
adversary. Say so in the rule's text, or the next audit over-credits it.

**MAX_PATH:** the remedy must name a short root. `D:/pd1wt/<lane>` worked today;
one under the temp path failed with "Filename too long".

## 5. Today

Install M1 tuned, plus its two-direction test. `pre-commit install` does not
cover this hook, so the per-checkout setup step must name it. Rewrite P6 as
what it becomes: *"An agent writing refs
in the main pdoom1 checkout is refused by `.git/hooks/reference-transaction`.
The refusal is bypassable, deliberately. Lanes get worktrees under
`D:/pd1wt/`."* Re-falsify by asserting the hook is installed and its test passes — not by
reading the reflog, which cannot answer.

issues.title: D4 ruling wanted: a sixth origin value (authored_art), and splitting the Manifund claim off NON_MODEL
issues.body:
**Drafted 2026-08-21 by the pdoom1-website seat, on Pip's ask. Nothing built; this is a ruling request.**

# D4 — a sixth origin value, and splitting the Manifund claim off `origin`

**Decision asked for.** A pixel artist is in prospect. Their first hand-drawn frame
has no honest home in the five-value `origin` vocabulary ruled 2026-08-11: not
model output, not markup-that-is-the-asset, not a render of code, not a
photograph — and `unknown` would be a lie, since we would know exactly who made
it and how. Two entangled rulings: **(1)** add one value, `authored_art`;
**(2)** stop `NON_MODEL` doing double duty, moving the Manifund claim out of
`origin` into a separately-ruled store defaulting to *unset*, rendering
**UNKNOWN**.

**Proposed value** — in the voice of the existing five:

```
authored_art       a person made the image itself with a drawing tool
```

**Proposed second field.** A new store `godot/data/art_commitment.json`, keyed by
pack-relative path, values `discharges` / `does_not_discharge`, written only by a
human ruling recording who/when/why. **Absent is the default and prints
`UNKNOWN -- not ruled`, never `no`.** A separate FILE, not a sixth key on the
asset record, for the D3 reason (separate stores beat one store with a
discriminator) *and* a mechanical one: a full `--write` rebuilds every record
from `classify()`, so a hand-ruled key inside the manifest is clobbered on the
next re-run. Not hypothetical — `--apply-credentials` and `--apply-authors` are
both narrow passes precisely because full re-runs are unsafe on your machine.

## What changes

- `tools/assets/backfill_provenance.py` — `ORIGIN_VALUES` gains `authored_art`;
  the ORIGIN VOCABULARY docstring gains the line above. `--record` validates
  against that list, so nothing else is needed to record the first frame.
- `classify()` — gains **no heuristic**. There is no evidence tier for "a person
  drew this" short of a human saying so. Instead a full `--write` must PRESERVE
  hand-attested records and print what it preserved, or the artist's frame
  silently reverts to `unknown` and loses its `author`.
- `godot/data/asset_provenance.json` — `_origin_values` grows on the next write.
  **No existing record changes.**
- `tools/assets/check_provenance.py` — the Manifund trigger reads the new store
  instead of `NON_MODEL`. Note the two path exclusions the trigger already
  carries (`cats/simple/`, `cats/default/`): those exist only to stop it firing
  on non-model assets that were never the milestone. They *are* the double duty,
  already patched by hand.
- Guards/tests: `--self-test` gains (a) unset renders UNKNOWN, not NO; (b) an
  `authored_art` record with no ruling fires "a ruling is owed", exit 0; (c) a
  full `--write` does not demote a recorded `authored_art` asset. Nothing new
  needs wiring — pre-commit `provenance-check` and `quality-checks.yml` already
  run both tools.
- `CREDITS.md` stays the author SSOT; `--apply-authors` already handles the
  artist's row. **No change to `author` semantics.**

## What could go wrong

1. **The full-write clobber.** Today a `--record`ed asset survives only until
   someone runs a full `--write`. If the preserve rule above is skipped, the
   artist's first frame becomes `unknown`, `check_provenance.py` reports "a NEW
   unattributable asset — the estate got worse", and the artist is erased by a
   routine re-run. Highest-probability failure here.
2. **A second store nobody fills.** Unset is legal, so the funder claim can sit
   UNKNOWN forever and no guard ever interrupts anyone. Mitigation is the
   "a ruling is owed" shout — but that is a shout, not a gate, by design.
3. **Vocabulary creep.** An artist repainting over a generated base is a hybrid
   `authored_art` describes badly, and a sixth value invites a seventh. Suggest
   ruling now that mixed lineage records the **last hand that changed it** plus
   `origin_detail`, never a new value.

## Rejected

- **`human`** — ruled out 2026-08-11; the 8 music `.ogg` are captures of
  hand-authored patches and are neither. Not reopened.
- **Reuse `authored_code`** — false (a raster frame is not markup), and it would
  join the Manifund set as a side effect.
- **Add `authored_art` to `NON_MODEL`** — makes a factual classification assert a
  claim to a funder. This proposal exists to stop that.
- **A `human_made` boolean on the record** — a boolean has no UNKNOWN, `false`
  reads as a denial, and credit is an open string, never a machine/human flag.
- **Derive discharge from `author != unattributed`** — an artist who asks not to
  be named would then fail to discharge a commitment they did discharge.
  Attribution is a duty to a person; disclosure is a claim to a funder.

issues.title: Playtest 655/C55: icon bar lands; cap the top bar at 10 buttons; three actions want submenus; mouse-over jiggle is a regression
issues.body:
**From:** coordination seat · **Source:** Pip voice memos `2026-08-06_080951__da695c39` and `_081345__1ef21992`, recorded 08:09 and 08:13 AEST playing the **655 / C55 action-visibility build**. Transcribed locally. Quotes are ASR output, lightly punctuated. This is live play, not a review pass.

## Core message

**The icon bar lands.** *"Having the icons along the top is great."* Fifteen buttons, only one wrapping. Most of what follows is refinement on a change he likes, plus one UI bug that is a regression of something already fixed once.

Two items are bigger than their bug reports: **a menu-depth problem in the action list**, and **a proposal to fix the top-bar width by capping button count rather than by handling overflow.**

## Cap the button count -- his proposal, and it is a design rule not a fix

> With the buttons aligned along the top like this, I think let's get our default numbering systems improved so that we have **no more than 10 buttons along the top** -- and that's including how many buttons we want to have unlocked in total, so we can kind of **lock ourselves into a UI width**.

So: **the total unlockable set is bounded by the bar, not the other way round.** That is a constraint on game design, not just layout -- if a new action would be the eleventh, something else has to become a submenu or the action does not ship. Worth deciding explicitly, because it is much cheaper to adopt now than after twenty actions exist.

## Menu depth -- three actions are in the wrong place

He named these while playing:

- **"Work your connections"** should sit under **hiring / HR**, not top level -- *"it feels like a way to get leads in a networking thing, so that should probably belong inside the networking function."*
- **"Onboarding"** (currently 5) -- same, should be a submenu.
- **Fundraising at number one** -- noted approvingly, no change.

This is the same pressure as the button cap: the top level is a scarce resource and currently holds things that are steps within other things.

## UI bugs

**1. Upgrade buttons jiggle on mouse-over -- and this is a regression.**

> something about the on-mouse-over effects causes all the buttons to jiggle up and down, in a way that reminds me that **we had solved this problem -- we'd had this problem before**.

He generalises it: *"there's a general phenomenon of mouse-over causing the UI effects to reorient themselves, which we'll need to work on, and it's particularly concentrated in the work around improving the upgrades."*

**Worth finding the original fix before writing a new one.** A previously-solved problem recurring in a new component usually means the fix lived in the component rather than in a shared rule.

**2. Upgrade panel scrolls when it should not need to.** *"It scrolls, which means we need to maybe make the upgrades come up on the left a little bit, so the top of the upgrade section can come up and there's more room for them."*

**3. `F3` risk overlay hides a whole tab.** Four sections exist -- game state, errors, performance, **controls** -- but *"controls is not there until you tab over to the right, so I'd like to extend the F3 functionality so that the bar pops out a little bit to the left."*

**4. Operations and Office share the same icon.** Two different menus, one glyph.

**5. Money disappears immediately with no feedback.** *"The money seems to disappear immediately. I'm noticing maybe we need an action log."* His suggestion: **an action log on the right-hand side of the plan screen**, so instantaneous actions leave a trace. He raised this twice in one session.

**6. Month review screen** -- *"still needs some work"*, no specifics, flagged as known.

## Not a real bug, but worth reading

He reached an unresolvable **employee burnout crisis** page and could not proceed: *"it says I cannot resolve events in phase one."* He is explicit about the cause and about it not counting:

> I accidentally generated an event during a planning phase with the controls to trigger a random event... so this has created a game-ending bug, which is kind of cool, but **also comes from fiddling around in the control overlay, so it's not a real problem**.

**Do not fix as reported.** But it does show a dev-tool action can put the game into a state the game cannot exit -- which is the dev-tool versus alpha-tool boundary from `#1112` showing up as a concrete failure. Either the control overlay should refuse to generate events in a phase that cannot resolve them, or the phase should handle events it did not expect. Worth a decision, not a patch.

## Things he liked, so they do not get refactored away

Operations having icons inside it (*"awesome"*); the loan menu having more options; the upgrade system at the bottom; computer-systems upgrade; the `F3` risk overlay itself (*"the dev command is awesome"*). He successfully adopted the cat.

Open question he raised without answering: the Office submenu items -- Office Tour, Office Co-working Corner, Walk Up Office, University Annex -- *"these are all buttons here, which is interesting, so I'm not quite sure where we're going with that."* Someone should say what that group is for.

## One item that is not for this repo

While looking at negative space on the planning screen he said he wants *"much better insight into when the next couple of workshops are"*, wants his **next few weeks as a developer scheduled out**, and *"especially once I figure out when my holiday is"*. He explicitly framed it as a reward for finishing the calendar work today.

**Coordination is taking that.** No action here.

## Standing note

The research-quality text block -- *"rushed / standard / thorough, baseline speed, no side effects"* -- is called out again: *"it's taking up a huge amount of space and it does nothing."* This matches `#1090`, still open. He is now annoyed by it in play rather than in review, which usually means it is due.
